title: Show HN: Hob - Open-source, on device alternative to Claude Cowork and ChatGPT
body:
Hey HN, I'm Christian and this is a new OSS project I've been noodling on for the last couple of weeks. Hob is a free, MIT-licensed desktop app for Mac, Windows and Linux that works on your files the way the Claude and ChatGPT desktop apps do, except the model runs on your own computer. It uses open-weight models (currently Gemma 4 and gpt-oss). All your chats and files never leave your system. The only things that go online are web search (can be turned off in settings) and any MCP connectors you add yourself.

Main features:

- Automatically finds the best open-weight model for your hardware on first install (Mac/Linux/Windows)

- Writes sandboxed Python code for ad hoc tools (data processing, document conversion, graphs etc.)

- Built-in web search (powered by SearXNG)

- MCP support

- Image recognition

- CRUD to your local filesystem

- Works fully offline with no internet

Before building this I tried every local AI app I could find, but it seemed each one had different problems. The main thing I noticed is that none of them could do what the ChatGPT and Claude apps do with your files, e.g. read and change files in a folder, look at images, run c

title: Show HN: Omnara – Open-source alternative to Claude Managed Agents
body:
Hey all, Kartik from Omnara (https://omnara.com) here. We're building an open-source API for running durable agents. You create an agent with an API call, and Omnara runs the agent loop, gives the agent sandboxes to run commands in, and handles secrets, permissions, and RBAC. Each agent's state is stored in Postgres, so agents survive restarts and cost nothing while idle. You can message them and stream their events over the API.

You may remember us from our early days, when we made a remote-control phone app for Claude Code and Codex. Since the harness ran on a laptop back then, we had to build a relay to reach it, it stopped when the laptop closed, and moving it to a cloud sandbox meant syncing code and agent state between machines. We didn't think remote-controlling a local agent was end-game for how people would run agents, so we built a new product where the agent runs in the cloud, any client can talk to it through an API, and it can still use your laptop as one of its machines.

Anthropic and OpenAI are building hosted versions of this, like Claude Managed Agents and the OpenAI Agents API. Omnara is an op

title: Open-source, cross-harness memory for AI agents
body:
Earlier this year, my co-founder and I found ourselves frequently switching between different coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) anytime we ran out of shaky usage limits or a newer, better model came out.

We became increasingly frustrated with having to re-explain our tasks, workflows, common mistake patterns, etc. anytime we switched agents. We found no good free alternatives out there, so we built our own and fully open-sourced it!

Beacon hooks into 20+ different agent harnesses, captures session telemetry (prompts, tool calls, command executions, etc) in one normalized format, and distills it into common patterns and repeatable workflows with a human-approval step. This compounded knowledge is then accessible to any future agent via skills / MCP.

We believe your agent data is yours to own and should not be locked behind any frontier lab's ecosystem or closed memory infrastructure. We built Beacon to make working across agents way more transparent and efficient.

Try it out and tell us what you think: https://github.com/Asymptote-Labs/agent-beacon

title: Show HN: KiviDB, a faster Redis-compatible memory database and vector cache
body:
Hi all,

So I have been working on this project KiviDB from February 2026. It started as a project for me to understand rust, having a product with no GC pauses, memory blow up after snapshots and getting OOM on running pods, and that was actually an issue I faced with Dragonfly. I wanted to have something picking the best of Rust, but also picking the best parts of other alternatives like Garnet and Dragonfly. I used AI a lot, but I was the one making the design decisions based on the tests that claude picked from my history of troubleshooting sessions as part of my job. KiviDB supports both RESP2 and RESP3 protocol. I had some founders credits on my AWS account which helped me with the infra, and running instances I could perform benchmark on.

Its keyspace is sharded across threads, it is multi-threaded in nature, and performs best on Linux due to io_uring, I used the tokio_uring crate for this. It also has tokio fallback for other OS's. title: Show HN: Death Plan Switch, a self-hosted dead man's switch for solo devs
body:
Hi HN,

I'm Peter Bishop and I've been working in graphics and web tech for over 25yrs.

I've recently launched Death Plan Switch to solve a major problem in my succession plan. What if I go missing or die? The right people are told and my business can continue to operate for my clients.

There's a backstory to this project, I was hospitalised in 2012 and lost my business back then and I couldn't get the data to my technical 2IC in time without frustrating my clients.

Death Plan Switch solves this problem, it's free to download and use or study under the MIT license.

I've been using it for the last few weeks. It was authored with the help of Claude Code after writing an extensive MD document and it passed 42 unit tests.

I hope you get some use out of it, or it inspires your own succession plans. My clients are telling me this is a strong sales feature when they trust me with their hosting and technology accounts.

Happy to answer any questions.

Kind regards, Peter Bishop.

title: Tell HN: I unknowingly broke the PHP RCE embargo. I am sorry
body:
I posted here about the then-upcoming PHP RCEs related to CVE-2026-109618 & CVE-2026-109619. I appreciate this has had considerable knock-on effects with the schedule for co-ordinated disclosure, and created additional workload.

I am truly sorry. I take full responsibility for my actions.

It was not remotely my intention to cause any of the subsequent side effects.

At the time of posting, I didn't know about any embargo. My contact had told me there was no embargo, and her contact had told her the same thing.

As someone who follows the 4-weekly PHP release cycle and compiles it from source, my intention was to alert others in a similar position to be aware of the importance/urgency of the updates.

That clearly backfired in a pretty wild fashion. I have learned my lesson.

body:
Just a quick notice for anyone using this software in their homelab. Tailscale has released **v1.104.4** to address a series of prominent vulnerabilities [disclosed last week](https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/unpatched-tailscale-ssh-flaws-could-let.html). These vulns affect the [Tailscale Serve](https://tailscale.com/docs/features/tailscale-serve) and [Tailscale SSH](https://tailscale.com/docs/features/tailscale-ssh) functionalities of the software, and allow already-authorized attackers to gain further privileges erroneously. Kindly update to that version or higher, especially if you are using one of the SSH/Serve features.

For [headscale](https://headscale.net/) selfhosters that also use Tailscale SSH, consider setting `TS_SSH_DISABLE_FORWARDING=1` on all clients, as headscale does not have a way to force turning off SSH forwarding (one of the attack vectors). Headscale also has a relevant disclosed vulnerability affecting node registration, and an in-progress patch for that which is trackable [here](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/3586/).

title: For people using OpnSense who want some automatic snapshots.
body:
So here is the deal.  OpnSense is based on FreeBSD (as the users know but others may not understand) and utilizes ZFS Snapshots which are an amazing way to go back to a previous state when something breaks after an update.  However for some reason the cron section has been changed so you can not add any random cron job and can only select from predefined options.  This means we have to work from the CLI to add jobs, but even worse after an update the cron jobs are removed.... which becomes self defeating.


I think I have a decent solution that will work to not only persist the backup script that will automatically create and remove snapshots but also recreate the cron jobs automatically.  Ideally there would be some sort of addon where we could adjust things but this is the best I can do for now and want to share with everyone.


Here is the script, place it at:  /usr/local/etc/rc.syshook.d/start/99-snapshot-addon.sh

title: OpenAI says it will no longer train its AI models on the live internet, citing 'significant risks' | TechCrunch
body:
On Friday, OpenAI said that it will train its models using cached copies and simulated versions of the internet instead of the live web because the models are too unpredictable to be trusted with live internet access.

The frontier lab announced its new policy two weeks after its rival, Anthropic, began limiting its newest and, in theory, most capable models from accessing the live internet. Researchers adopted these policies after months of incidents in which models pursuing training tasks broke into external systems in search of answers, collaborated on obscure message boards, and developed exotic hacking strategies.

A comprehensive redesign

The app's bottom bar now has three sections: Discover for browsing, Search for queries and quick access to categories, and My Apps for tracking installed apps, updates, and issues.

You will also find that the Settings menu has moved to the top-right, being placed alongside the new Repositories menu.

Coming back to the Discover page, it has been configured to highlight newly added apps, recently updated ones, and the most downloaded ones in the repository. Related categories are grouped together, making it easier to browse the full catalog without getting lost in a long list.

Just so you know, the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI) represents around 8,000 music labels across 70 countries.

In its submission to the EU's Counterfeit and Piracy Watch List consultation, the group calls yt-dlp "a major problem for the music industry" and names four of its maintainers by their GitHub handles.

A Piracy Watch List?

Run by the European Commission's Directorate-General for Trade and Economic Security, the Watch List identifies online services and physical marketplaces outside the EU reported to engage in or facilitate copyright infringement.

While it sounds serious, the undertaking isn't meant to gather legal findings and does not mandate any form of direct action. It's closer to a naming exercise intended to pressure operators and governments outside the EU into addressing the identified services.

The 2027 edition is being compiled from submissions received through September 2026, with the final list expected in Q2 2027.

title: Open Source OS That Are Not Linux
body:
Every system listed below is open source and not powered by Linux. Each has an ISO or installer you can boot today, and many of the picks can even run Linux applications.

Think of it as a list of operating systems that are friends with Tux but not friendly enough to call him inside for a cup of tea.

This list is not ranked.

Vinix

If you own an Apple Silicon MacBook and want a system that is neither macOS nor a Linux distribution, Vinix is aimed at you. Only the original M1 is supported today, and Alexander Medvednikov, the author of V, maintains the project.

The kernel is monolithic and written mostly in V, while part of it is C and assembly. Because memory is managed by hand, no garbage collector can interrupt a system call, and the security model borrows certain concepts from OpenBSD.

On ARM64, it runs Alpine Linux binaries natively, and pkg installs packages from Alpine's aarch64 repositories. ISOs for both x86-64 and ARM64 are available for virtual machine use.

A good pick if you enjoy poking at experimental kernels.

title: Mozilla Thunderbird 157 Fixes 100% CPU Usage, OpenPGP, and IMAP Issues
body:
Thunderbird 157 is now available, bringing a long list of fixes across mail handling, authentication, encryption, calendars, and account setup, along with a couple of new controls aimed at enterprise deployments.

One notable fix addresses an issue where Thunderbird’s status bar could remain active after an operation finished, potentially pushing CPU usage to 100%. The release also fixes cases where the message list displayed the wrong sender and where sent messages silently failed to save to the IMAP Sent folder.

OpenPGP users get several improvements. Thunderbird 157 fixes an issue that could cause valid RSA OpenPGP keys to be rejected and prevent encryption. Key discovery can now correctly locate replacement keys after an existing key is revoked. The client can also display remote content in OpenPGP messages encrypted with integrity protection.

On the authentication side, intermittent Gmail OAuth2 failures on Windows have been addressed, along with SMTP OAuth2 problems caused by large access tokens. Exchange users should see more reliable NTLM authentication after password changes. Another fix targets SMTP AUTH LOGIN failures following username challenges.

title: Wine on OpenBSD? Yes, and It Can Already Run The Witcher 3
body:
A bit of a surprise, really, Wine is making its way to OpenBSD. An experimental port has been submitted, and early testing shows it can already run dozens of 64-bit Windows apps (including quite a few games).

The announcement comes from OpenBSD developer Thomas Frohwein, who made the proposed port public on the OpenBSD mailing list and describes it as possibly the most surprising port proposal of the year.

As Frohwein makes clear, getting Wine to work on OpenBSD has been a team effort with the bulk of the work being done by Andrii and Fabien. The biggest hurdle has been the %gs segment register. Wine needs this, but OpenBSD doesn’t allow applications to set GSBASE directly.

The breakthrough was a software workaround which uses the %gs prefix to generate the instructions, circumventing a major compatibility issue which had previously made getting Wine onto the OS so difficult.

The results are already very impressive. The dev team has successfully tested a good number of 64-bit Windows apps, and most run quite nicely. title: ReactOS Can Now Be Installed & Used With Its NTFS Driver
body:
The ReactOS open-source operating system has seen its NTFS file-system driver mature to the point that it can be finally used for installing and using ReactOS with it. NTFS formatting support is also finally now possible with this driver too.

Hitting this major milestone of its NTFS driver maturing to the point of installing and using the ReactOS operating system itself with it also puts the project one step closer to its elusive beta release.

ReactOS posted to X today this big goal being realized of the NTFS driver being much more mature for handling ReactOS installations.

It is important to note though that the ReactOS NTFS driver still lacks caching leading to slower performance than other NTFS drivers/platforms, journaling, and security support are also not yet implemented. There is also the possibility of other undiscovered bugs they note.

A nice milestone for ReactOS and the latest in a variety of nice achievements they have made so far in 2026.

title: Let's Encrypt to Cut SSL Certificate Lifetimes to 64 Days in February 2027
body:
Let’s Encrypt, the free and open certificate authority widely used to secure websites with HTTPS, announced it will shorten the default validity period of its TLS certificates from 90 days to 64 days, starting February 10, 2027.

All certificates issued or renewed from that date will have a 64-day lifespan unless users explicitly select one of the shorter options already available: 45 or six days.

Existing certificates will remain valid until their expiration dates. Let’s Encrypt expects the final 90-day certificate to expire on May 11, 2027. The organization also confirmed no valid certificates will be revoked during the transition.

To help administrators prepare, Let’s Encrypt will introduce 64-day certificates in its staging environment on October 14, 2026, allowing users to test their renewal setups before the change reaches production.

The move is part of a broader effort to improve web security by reducing how long compromised or incorrectly issued certificates remain usable. Simply put, shorter certificate lifetimes mean attackers have less time to exploit a stolen private key.

title: LiberNT: New ReactOS Fork Aims for Windows 11 Compatibility
body:
The LiberNT project is working on an alternative implementation of the Windows NT architecture, using Windows 11 version 24H2 as its compatibility reference. Unlike Linux distributions, LiberNT does not use the Linux kernel. It builds on the ReactOS codebase while replacing and extending several core components.

One of the project’s main priorities is ARM64 support, particularly for single-board computers and embedded devices. LiberNT also supports x86-64 and 32-bit x86, while RISC-V 64-bit and PowerPC ports are under development.

According to the developers, the implementation follows a clean-room approach. Windows behavior is studied using Microsoft’s public documentation, SDK and WDK headers, public symbols, and black-box testing. The team states no proprietary Windows code is copied or transcribed.

On the technical side, one of the biggest changes is NVS, a new memory manager and kernel pool implementation replacing the corresponding ReactOS components. LiberNT also introduces a new cache manager, with developers claiming better results than the original ReactOS memory manager in their memory and cache benchmarks.

title: Transmission 4.1.4 Open-Source BitTorrent Client Released with Various Fixes
body:
Transmission 4.1.4 has been released today as the fourth maintenance update to the latest Transmission 4.1 series for this popular open-source BitTorrent client, a bugfix release that fixes various issues.

Coming almost four months after Transmission 4.1.3, which was a small update fixing a CORS bug that leaked the anti-CSRF nonce, a use-after-free bug in peer code, and a build error when compiling with fmt 12.2.0, the Transmission 4.1.4 release hardens the torrent-add RPC method against malformed requests.

Transmission 4.1.4 also fixes a regression introduced in Transmission 4.1 that could cause torrents with zero-byte files to be handled incorrectly, which could sometimes cause downloaded progress to be lost, and fixes a rare bug that could leave Transmission hung but running on it is closed.

title: I built a free and open-source desktop app for organizing table tennis tournaments
body:
Hi! I’m a table tennis player, club captain and referee who apparently decided that what the world desperately needed was another tournament manager.

So I made LibreTT. 🏓

It’s a desktop app for running table tennis tournaments: players, registrations, fees, groups, draws, matches, knockout brackets, results, backups and exports. It runs on Linux, Windows and macOS, works offline and requires no account.

So why another one?

Because I don’t think competition data should belong to the software that records it.

A result is created by players, clubs, referees and organizers. The software is just a tool. If LibreTT disappears tomorrow, your tournament history shouldn’t disappear with it.

That’s why LibreTT is licensed under AGPL-3.0-or-later. No subscriptions, activation servers, paid feature tiers or vendor lock-in. The source is public, the data stays local, and the community should always be able to preserve, move and continue its own infrastructure.

This is the first public beta (0.1.0-beta.1), so the next milestone is testing it against its natural predator: an actual tournament organizer who is 15 minutes behind schedule.

title: Court Agrees with EFF: Utah’s VPN Law Demands a Technical Impossibility
body:
When state lawmakers attempt to rewrite how the internet works, users rely on courts to recognize that laws can’t make technical impossibilities a reality. That’s why we were happy to see that a court has blocked Utah’s attempt to outlaw the privacy protections of Virtual Private Networks (VPNs). 

In a win for digital rights, a federal judge has issued a preliminary injunction blocking Utah’s SB 73, the state’s draconian anti-VPN age verification law. The decision comes as EFF submitted our comments to the Utah Department of Commerce, detailing how forcing platforms to detect and block privacy-preserving tools undermines user privacy and security worldwide while demanding the impossible.  
What SB 73 Does 

Signed into law earlier this year, SB 73 attempted to regulate adult websites by requiring them to block VPN users or to identify the physical location of visitors using them or similar tools that mask their network traffic. It even went so far as to prohibit websites from offering instructions on how to use a VPN to bypass these checks. This made Utah, to EFF’s knowledge, the first state in the nation to target the use of VPNs to avoid legally mandated age-verification gates.

EFF brought a lawsuit against the US government over social media AI powered mass surveilence. The Government tried to dismiss the suit on multiple grounds. Lack of standing, lack of of injury, pre-enforcement, and others.

The EFF prevailed on every point. The suit against the administration can go forward. Whether EFF prevails on the merits of the case, we will see. But it is a good start. The court was sympathetic to the EFF's arguments so far.

> The court disagreed, explaining that “Plaintiffs’ allegations are of an ongoing surveillance program that is actively chilling the speech of their members and otherwise causing harm.” That chilling effect is a First Amendment injury even if there isn’t a direct prohibition on speech. Please resist the pull of thinking that even if the EFF wins the case, it is useless b/c it does not solve *every* privacy problem. We will never have a single nail to strike with a single hammer. There are many battles in the war for privacy. The more won, the better.

title: Court finds ALPR (Flock) was an unconstitutional search & 4A violation. (positive news)
body:
I made up the title b/c the URL is to the court's finding. Doesn't have a title per se.

TLDR (ruling is 38 pages, so this is BRIEF gd!)

Driver was stopped for following too close. Officer gave warning, but no citation. Officer ran ALPR history, then searched car based on ALPR. Driver admitted to having marijuana in the vehicle, which officer said he didn't care about, and was only after hard drugs. ALPR history had driver driving a long distance for a short visit to the state.

Court ruled:

1. Traffic stop was legal and justified by observed violation. Officer had reasonable basis to stop driver.

2. The subsequent search was NOT constitutional, since officer did not have a warrant for ALPR data, and had no reasonable suspicion of criminal activity.

Result from ruling,

> (Driver) has a reasonable expectation of privacy in the location data which tracked her movements over several weeks. .... The ALPR search was an unreasonable governmental intrusion of protected privacy rights.

Vehicle search result was quashed.

title: Require Police to Get a Warrant to Search ALPR Data
body:
> Automated license plate readers (ALPRs) are mass surveillance. They photograph every passing car and log where and when it was captured, building a searchable record of where nearly everyone drives. Cities should not buy them, and cities that already have them should shut them down.
> 
> Where these systems still operate, courts and state legislatures must reduce their harms by (among other things) requiring police to get a warrant before searching stored ALPR data. A warrant requirement would not make mass surveillance acceptable, but it would require police to justify a search to a judge before accessing records of people’s movements. Without this independent judicial check on police power, officers have been searching this data for improper reasons (many exposed by EFF) that violate our fundamental rights.

title: systemd Officially Adds Rust Support for New Components
body:
EEE

>The systemd project has officially introduced support for developing programs in Rust, following the merger of a pull request submitted by Linux kernel developer Christian Brauner. The change, merged into the project’s main branch, establishes a new development option for systemd while keeping its existing C-based architecture intact.

>And before anyone assumes systemd is preparing a complete rewrite in Rust, that’s not the case. The maintainers agreed on a deliberately limited approach: Rust may be used only for new, standalone components that other parts of systemd do not depend on. Existing C code will remain untouched.

>Another important decision concerns the build process. Rather than introducing Cargo, Rust’s standard package manager and build tool, systemd continues to use Meson for all builds. This keeps Rust development integrated into the project’s existing build infrastructure.

>The implementation also places strict limits on dependencies. Rust programs use the no_std approach, meaning they do not rely on Rust’s standard library or external third-party crates. Instead, they interact with systemd’s existing C libraries through generated bindings.

title: Linux 7.4 Sound Changes Merged: "The AI Flood Continues"
body:
Linux sound subsystem maintainer Takashi Iwai of SUSE began the Linux 7.4 sound pull request by noting that "the AI flood continues" with there continuing to be a lot of new patches coming as a result of AI/LLM agents devising patches as well as uncovering new kernel bugs.

Takashi went on to explain that it was another busy cycle with changes in the sound subsystem from lots of core code hardening to new platforms and codecs as well. The core ALSA code has been hardened against some race conditions, there's a buffer leak fix in the compression offload code, race fixes in the JACK code, and other race conditions and more typical C bug fixes. The OSS sequencer emulation code has also been marked as deprecated for Linux 7.4.

On the hardware side, the Linux 7.4 sound updates include support for compressed audio playback on SOF IPC4 with Intel Tigerlake and newer. There is also AMD ACP 7.0/7.F sound IP support with SoundWire and the PDM controller. The new AMD ACP 7.0/7.F IP appears for upcoming Ryzen Zen 6 platforms.

There are also quirks for many different Intel/AMD laptops from the likes of Lenovo, ASUS, HP, AAcer, HONOR, MSI, and others.

New codec drivers are for the ESS ES9039Q

title: Alternative to Docker Content Trust (and cosign)?

 We've been using  DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST=1  and  rsync to manually pin the keys  for the debian image layers we download with  docker pull . This had the effect of disabling TOFU. That's important because, if we don't pin the certificates manually with rsync, then docker would happily pull a malicious image (and the malicious singing keys at the same time, from mallory). By pinning the keys before ever running  docker pull , that's the only way we can get docker to detect a malicious image (not signed by the key we expect) on an ephemeral build machine. 
 Unfortunately, I just discovered that the official docker documentation says that DCT is being deprecated. Apparently this was announced last year, and in June this blog post was published with advice:

Hey HN, this is Andy from Respan (https://www.respan.ai). We are building an open-source Rust AI gateway. It is a decoupled gateway, so everything is a plugin, including different providers, protocols (MCP, voice), modalities (images, videos), and gateway features (fallbacks, PII redaction, smart routing).

Hi HN, we're Ahnaf and Seungmin from Simantic (https://simantic.com). We are building the simulation layer that lets engineers and AI agents test and validate firmware without hardware.

Before Simantic, we were ex-firmware engineers at companies like Neuralink and Tesla. We’ve worked on some of the coolest projects, like the Cybertruck and Roadster, back when they were still early prototypes.

We started working on firmware back when ChatGPT didn’t exist yet, but over the years, we saw how much of the engineering and development work has been automated as the frontier models improved to this point. In software, AI can run and test code inside your computer in a matter of seconds. But as firmware engineers, we didn’t have that luxury. title: Show HN: AstroHelm – Use your phone camera to aim a telescope or telephoto lens
body:
Hello HN!

As an amateur astronomer living in New York City, finding objects in the night sky has always been a huge challenge. I thought about using the smartphone's gyroscope and magnetometer, but the accuracy left a lot to be desired.

Then I learned about plate solving: given a picture of the sky, we can determine exactly where in the sky the camera was pointing by identifying the star pattern. This was a much better fit - as long as the phone and the optics are rigidly connected, we can repeatedly photograph the sky and determine the pointing direction with very high accuracy.

A lot of work was done to design an algorithm that works reliably with smartphone cameras, which have limited light sensitivity and wider field of view which includes buildings and trees. I experimented a lot with machine learning, and to my surprise, traditional CV methods actually performed better at extracting stars from the image.

The result is AstroHelm, an iOS and Android app that helps figure out where your telescope or camera is pointing, and guides you to the object of your choice. Just follow an arrow on screen, and the object will land right in your eyepiece or viewfinder. Everythin

title: Show HN: Certo – An open source platform to deliver Open Badges
body:
Certo is open-source infrastructure for issuing, managing, verifying, and exchanging digital credentials.

It implements Open Badges 3.0[1] and W3C Verifiable Credentials[2] which are the open standards that make credentials portable, machine-verifiable, and vendor-independent.

It is designed to be:

- Self-hosted: run it inside your own infrastructure, air-gapped network, or sovereign cloud - Standards-compliant: credentials it issues work with any OB3/VC-compatible system - API-first: everything the UI can do, the API can do - Exportable: your data is always yours, in open formats - Extensible: a small, stable core with a plugin interface for everything else

A demo is available at https://certo.schroedinger-hat.org/ which we're using for Schrödinger Hat[3] conferences, workshops, partner communities.

I'll be around if you have any questions. Feel free to give a feedback on the project.

[1] https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/ob/v3p0 [2]

title: Create, preview, and edit files directly in the Gemini app
body: We’re introducing new ways to create and refine files and code in the Gemini app. You can now generate, preview, and edit files right within your Gemini app chat—expand to full screen to type edits directly, highlight text to ask questions, or have Gemini refine them. PDF preview and editing is supported on both the web and mobile, while all other formats (documents, spreadsheets, slide decks, Markdown files, TXT files, and code) are supported on the web only. Here are just some of the new things you can do:      Generate and refine slide decks:  Create presentation outlines or slide content, preview the layout in chat, and edit directly or ask Gemini to adjust the tone and structure before opening in Google Slides, or downloading as a PPTX or PDF.   Build and export Google Sheets:  Generate structured trackers, tables, and data models from a prompt, preview them in Gemini, and open them directly in Google Sheets.   Edit documents and PDFs:  Quickly draft PDFs, Google Docs, LaTeX, Markdown, or TXT files, and make manual or prompted edits inline on web or in a full-screen view—plus you can upload all of them to Drive. title: Immersive explorations now available in the Gemini app
body: We’re introducing a library of  immersive explorations  in the Gemini app, giving users an interactive, visual way to explore topics layer-by-layer, from microscopic systems to deep space. Users can access this library in the  Gemini student hub  by clicking on “Try immersive explorations” and will soon be able to access  these immersive explorations  directly in a chat conversation with Gemini.  Whether it’s tracing trade routes on the Silk Road, peering inside a jet engine, or studying the physics of lightning, each scene unfolds into interactive nodes with guided explanations. Users can tap a layer to dig deeper, journeying from sweeping planetary scales straight down to molecules and atoms. Immersive explorations will soon include audio narration to walk users through each layer.  This feature is available on web and mobile to all users in the following languages: English, Indonesian, Hindi, Brazilian Portuguese, French, and simplified Chinese. Users in all other languages currently receive an English-only experience, with more languages coming soon.         Getting started      Admins:  There is no admin control for this feature. title: Apply compact form layout for pivot tables in Google Sheets
body: Google Sheets now supports compact form layout for pivot tables, which keeps multi-level pivot tables readable while reducing excessive horizontal scrolling. You can choose a layout directly from the pivot table editor:      Outline form:  each row field is displayed in its own column   Compact form:  all row fields are nested in a single column, with indentation and inline expand/collapse buttons showing the hierarchy     Compact form support also comes with enhanced Microsoft Excel import compatibility. Previously, importing Excel files containing compact form pivot tables into Sheets would convert them to outline form, changing the structure of the pivot table. Now, the source layout is preserved on import and maintained if the file is exported back to Excel.                 Switching a pivot table to compact form layout in Google Sheets      Getting started      Admins:  There is no admin control for this feature. title: Fill with Gemini now provides cell-level citations for web sources and supports larger requests
body: We are making it easier to verify your AI-generated data and scale your workflows in Google Sheets. When you use the AI function to generate cell values, Gemini will now provide the exact web sources referenced directly within each individual cell. This cell-level source attribution gives you full visibility to audit, verify, and cross-reference outputs for greater trust and accuracy. Sources are attributed to each individual cell and are available in Google Sheets on the web.  In addition, upgraded processing delivers faster response times and improved cell-over-cell consistency, performing up to 55 times faster than manual entry for 500 cell tasks*. Combined with expanded capacity supporting up to 3,000 cells per request, you can summarize, categorize, and process more data in a single request.   *Data based on a 95-participant internal study comparing manual entry against Fill with Gemini on a 500-cell task using English prompts for English language users. body: Gemini Notebook is now also available as a  Connected App  in the Gemini app. This new integration allows you to manage and query notebooks directly within your chats using natural language. title: Extract audio tracks in Google Vids
body: We are introducing the ability to decouple and extract the audio track from video clips directly within  Google Vids . By separating audio from video, creators gain granular control over multimedia editing, making it simple to custom-tailor voiceovers, remove distracting background noise, and align tracks across scenes.  Previously, video tracks could only be muted or unmuted as a single entity and were strictly scene-bound. With this update, you can extract a video's audio as a standalone clip that can play under other video tracks or span freely across multiple scenes on your timeline.  Key capabilities include:      Single-click extraction:  Instantly separate any video clip’s audio track into a standalone audio clip on the timeline.   Independent timeline editing:  Trim, move, or delete the detached audio track independently of your video footage without disrupting clip timing.     Getting started      Admins:  There is no admin control for this feature.   End users:  There is no end user setting for this feature. This update gives creators precise control over pacing and scene timing, streamlining video editing so teams can optimize storytelling, improve audience engagement, and deliver polished messages without relying on third-party editing software.  Whether presenting a fast-paced software walkthrough or slowing down technical steps, video speed controls make scene fine-tuning seamless. title: Real-time speech translation in Google Meet expands to 63 languages with automatic language detection
body: Gemini-powered speech translation in Google Meet will now support 63 languages across web and mobile devices (Android and iOS), with listening support on Google Meet hardware devices.  Previously, speech translation supported a limited set of language pairs and required configuring a single language pair for the entire meeting. With this update, powered by Gemini 3.5 Live Translate, participants can translate speech between any combination of the 63 supported languages in the same meeting with minimal configuration, helping global and distributed teams collaborate more naturally across language barriers.  We’re changing and simplifying how participants use speech translation during a multilingual call:      Automatic spoken language detection:  Meet automatically detects the language being spoken and translates it into each listener's preferred language in near real-time, even when multiple languages are spoken in the same meeting or when a speaker switches languages. title: Create box and whisker charts in Google Sheets
body: Google Sheets now natively supports box and whisker charts, a statistical chart type that shows how a dataset is distributed. Select a range of raw numeric values and Sheets calculates the minimum, first quartile, median, third quartile, maximum, mean, and outliers for you, with no helper formulas needed. You can choose inclusive or exclusive quartile calculation and show or hide inner points, outliers, mean markers, and mean lines.  Box and whisker support also comes with enhanced Microsoft Excel import compatibility. Previously, importing Excel files containing box and whisker charts into Sheets would drop the chart entirely. Now, these charts are preserved on import with their data references, calculations, and formatting intact, and charts created in Sheets export back to Excel as editable box and whisker charts. body: Following our  original feature announcement  for the web, we are excited to expand video tile pairing in Google Meet to both iOS and Android mobile devices. This update allows users to pair their video tile with another meeting participant, ensuring both tiles are displayed side-by-side for other attendees.  Tile pairing is particularly valuable for accessibility, giving participants who are Deaf or hard of hearing (HoH) the capability to pair their video tile with a sign language interpreter. By empowering users to keep both tiles visible in the same frame, regardless of who is speaking, video calls can be a more inclusive experience for all participants.  Whether you are co-presenting a session or requiring interpretation services, this mobile expansion ensures that important visual connections remain intact, even when you are on the go. Once paired, meeting participants will see both video tiles highlighted and positioned together in the meeting layout, with live captions displayed and attributed to both speakers. Users can discover apps and add skills to automate repetitive workflows such as adapting to your personal writing style or adhering to specific formatting guidelines.   Bringing custom skills and connected apps together into a unified space makes it easy to discover and manage how you customize your experience when using Gemini. title: Amazon Bedrock expands API support and introduces Cross-Region Inferencing for OpenAI models in AWS GovCloud (US)
body:
Amazon Bedrock now supports the OpenAI GPT-5.6 models (Terra and Luna) on the bedrock-runtime endpoint, with support for the Responses, Converse, and Chat Completions APIs in AWS GovCloud (US). It also adds support for Cross-Region Inference, allowing customers to use Cross-Region Inference within AWS GovCloud (US) regions to access higher throughput and increased redundancy.    
 Cross-Region Inference automatically routes inference requests across both AWS GovCloud (US) Regions to give you higher throughput, without you needing to manage capacity across multiple Regions. Cross-Region Inference within AWS GovCloud (US) routes requests across both regions so you can scale while maintaining US data sovereignty, giving you the broadest access to Bedrock capacity and the highest throughput during demand spikes. This launch also expands API support; you can use OpenAI GPT models with the Responses API, Chat Completions API, and the Converse API on the bedrock-runtime endpoint. title: Web Search now available on Kiro in AWS GovCloud (US)
body:
Kiro web search gives the agent real-time access to current information on the internet, so its answers draw on up-to-date search results and page content. The agent uses web search automatically when a question involves recent changes or topics beyond the model's training data. Answers that use web results include citations.  
 Kiro enterprise administrators can turn off web search and web fetch for their organization from the Kiro console under Settings. Teams can also remove web tools from individual custom agents, or block them with capability-based permission rules.  
 For more details, visit the  AWS GovCloud (US) documentation , the  monitoring and tracking guide , or contact your AWS account team. To learn more about Kiro, visit the  Kiro product page .

title: Amazon Connect Customer automatically saves in-progress emails as drafts
body: Amazon Connect Customer automatically saves in-progress emails as drafts, helping agents resume work without losing progress when connectivity is interrupted or when their browser is accidentally closed or refreshed. When agents return, their drafts are restored with the message body, recipients, subject line, and attachment references intact. Customers can also access saved draft data in their Amazon S3 buckets to build integrations with other applications.

title: Daybreak Red from OpenAI now available to eligible customers on Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US-East)
Amazon CloudFront now provides viewer ISP and post-quantum TLS details
body:
Amazon CloudFront can now forward two new optional headers to your origin. The CloudFront-Viewer-ISP header contains the name of the viewer's internet service provider (ISP), so you can see which network a request came from. The CloudFront-Viewer-TLS-Details header describes the cryptography used on each viewer's TLS connection, so you can see whether a connection used post-quantum cryptography (PQC).  
 With CloudFront-Viewer-ISP, you can break down traffic and performance by network. You can also isolate unusual traffic from a single provider. CloudFront-Viewer-TLS-Details includes the key exchange, signature scheme, and signature public key type for each connection. You can use it to measure the share of viewers that actually connect with PQC and identify clients that do not yet do so. To forward either header to your origin, add it to an origin request policy and attach the policy to your distribution.  
 To get started, see  adding CloudFront headers  and  controlling origin requests with a policy  in the Amazon CloudFront Developer Guide

title: Amazon MSK now supports TLS 1.3 for data in transit
body:
Amazon MSK now supports version 1.3 of Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol for MSK Provisioned clusters through encryption policies. TLS 1.3 delivers faster, more secure encryption for streaming data and is increasingly required by compliance frameworks and enterprise security standards. It is also one of the prerequisites for post-quantum cryptography for protecting data against attacks that collect encrypted traffic now with the intent to decrypt it later.  
 Customers can opt in to TLS 1.3 by selecting a named security policy in their MSK cluster configuration, with no change to existing clusters until a policy is applied. A named security policy defines which TLS version and cipher suites a cluster can accept. With this launch, Amazon MSK provides a set of policies customers can select and any connection that does not meet the selected policy requirements is rejected. This allows customers to stay in control of their security and compliance posture. Policies that support both TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 allow connections to negotiate the highest version the client supports allowing clients that support TLS 1.3 to connect on it immediately while clients on TLS 1.2 continue to connec

title: Amazon RDS for Oracle no longer requires automatic minor version upgrades for JVM, Spatial, Locator, and OLAP options
body:
Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for Oracle  now lets you turn off automatic minor version upgrades on new and existing DB instances that use the JVM, Spatial, Locator, or OLAP option. Previously, these options required automatic minor version upgrades to be enabled.  
 With this change, you decide when to apply minor version upgrades to DB instances using these options. If you turn off automatic minor version upgrades, we recommend that you apply new minor versions regularly so your DB instances keep the latest Oracle security fixes. To keep automatic minor version upgrades turned on and still control the order in which your environments are upgraded, you can use  AWS Organizations upgrade rollout policy .  
 This change is available in  all commercial AWS Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions  where Amazon RDS for Oracle is available. To learn more about options available in Amazon RDS for Oracle, see  Adding options to Oracle DB instances  in the Amazon RDS User Guide.

title: AWS WAF announces automatic SDK integration for Amazon CloudFront distributions
body: AWS WAF announces automatic SDK integration for Amazon CloudFront distributions. When you enable it, CloudFront adds the script tag for the AWS WAF JavaScript SDK to the HTML it serves, with no change to your application code, build process, or deployment. The SDK supplies the client-side signals used by three AWS WAF managed rule groups: Bot Control at the targeted inspection level, Fraud Control account takeover prevention (ATP), and Fraud Control account creation fraud prevention (ACFP).    Previously, supplying those signals required you to add a script tag to every page of every application you wanted to protect, and to maintain that tag across releases. For teams running many applications, or serving pages produced by systems they do not control, this created recurring work and a common source of misconfiguration, where a protection was enabled in AWS WAF but the client-side integration was missing. Enabling automatic SDK integration on the web ACL protecting your CloudFront distribution removes that per-application work.    Automatic SDK integration is available for web ACLs that are used with Amazon CloudFront and contain at least one of those managed rule groups. You can c

title: Amazon Connect Customer now supports versioning and aliasing for flows
body:
Amazon Connect Customer now supports versioning and aliasing for flows and flow modules, simplifying how you build, test, and deploy customer experience flows while minimizing impact to live end-customer traffic. With this launch, you can now create immutable versions of a flow and attach one or more friendly names (i.e., aliases) to a version, then point resources such as queues, quick connects, and phone numbers at an alias instead of a specific version.  
 Rolling out a new version takes a single update, with no need to republish or relink each resource. For example, you can publish an updated customer experience flow as a new version and validate it in a test environment while live traffic stays on the current version, then repoint the production alias to move every phone number to the new version in a single update.  
 This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Connect Customer is offered. To learn more, see  Flow versioning and aliasing  in the Amazon Connect Customer Administrator Guide. To learn more about Amazon Connect Customer, an agentic AI solution that helps enterprises deliver exceptional customer experiences, visit the  Amazon Connect Customer website

title: Managed Prometheus collectors now support Amazon MSK consumer-group metrics
body:
Managed Prometheus collectors now support Amazon MSK consumer-group metrics for  Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus  and  Amazon CloudWatch . The integration collects Kafka exporter metrics and consumer-group lag metrics from your Amazon MSK clusters. 
 Managed Prometheus collectors discover and collect Prometheus metrics from your workloads, so you don't run and operate collection agents yourself. You ingest the collected metrics into an Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus workspace or into Amazon CloudWatch, where you query and analyze them. You monitor Kafka stream health and consumer performance with consumer-group metrics. This helps you detect processing bottlenecks in your streaming applications. 
 This feature is available in all  AWS Regions  where managed Prometheus collectors are generally available. To learn more, see the documentation for  Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus  and  Amazon CloudWatch .

title: AWS Glue Data Catalog now supports Apache Iceberg table optimization in the US West (N. California) Region
body:
AWS Glue Data Catalog now supports automatic table optimization for Apache Iceberg tables in the US West (N. California) Region. Apache Iceberg is an open table format that delivers fast query performance over large tables in data lakes. With this launch, you can enable table optimization for individual tables or for all tables in your Data Catalog.  
 Apache Iceberg tables accumulate small files, snapshots, and unreferenced files with every write, which slows queries and increases storage costs over time. Table optimization continuously monitors your tables to compact small files in the background, remove snapshots that are past your retention settings, and delete unreferenced files that are no longer needed. You can monitor each run from the AWS Glue console, Amazon CloudWatch metrics, and logs.  
 You can enable table optimization using the AWS Glue console, AWS CLI, or AWS SDKs. For the full list of Regions where table optimization is available, see  Supported Regions for table optimizers . To learn more, see  Optimizing Iceberg tables  in the AWS Glue Developer Guide. To get started, visit the  AWS Glue product page .

title: Amazon SageMaker AI inference now supports GPU partitioning for real-time endpoints
body:
Amazon SageMaker AI inference now supports GPU partitioning, enabling you to run several models on a single GPU instead of dedicating a whole accelerator to each one. Using NVIDIA Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology, SageMaker AI divides a GPU into as many as seven isolated partitions, each with its own memory and compute. Customers serving small and mid-size models, such as fine-tuned variants, embedding models, rerankers, and classifiers, previously had to give every model an entire accelerator, so an instance hosted no more models than it had GPUs and paid for GPU capacity those models could never use. 
 With GPU partitioning, you choose how to divide the GPUs behind your endpoint and place each model on a partition sized to fit it. Several models then share one accelerator with hardware-enforced isolation, so a busy model cannot take memory or throughput from the models beside it. Right-sizing an accelerator to a workload also opens up newer instance generations that would otherwise be more capacity than a single model needs. title: AWS Marketplace now enables partners to list once and sell through multiple subsidiary accounts
body:
Today, AWS announces that AWS partners who operate multiple legal entities can publish a product listing once in their primary account and enable their local subsidiaries to sell it through direct private offers — eliminating the need to recreate and maintain duplicate listings across every account.  
 From the primary account, which retains ownership of the listing, partners authorize which products each subsidiary can sell and which buyer countries it can extend private offers to. Each subsidiary transacts under its own local tax identity, selects the local currencies it supports, and sets its own disbursement preferences and bank account. The AWS Marketplace insights report in the primary account provides a consolidated view of offers, agreements, and renewals across all connected subsidiary accounts. Partners can revoke a subsidiary authorization or a subsidiary connection at any time, which immediately stops that subsidiary from creating new offers — agreements and offers already extended to buyers remain unchanged.  
 This capability is available today at no additional cost in all AWS Regions where AWS Marketplace is available. To get started, see   Managing subsidiary a

title: Amazon RDS for Oracle and SQL Server now support storage autoscaling on additional storage volumes
body:
Amazon RDS for SQL Server   and   Amazon RDS for Oracle   now support RDS storage autoscaling on  additional storage volumes . RDS storage autoscaling automatically scales storage capacity in response to growing database workloads, with zero downtime.  
 Additional storage volumes allow you to add up to three additional volumes to increase your storage capacity up to 256 TiB. Previously, you had to manually provision storage capacity on the additional storage volumes based on anticipated application capacity demands while autoscaling could be enabled on the primary storage volume. Under-provisioning could result in application downtime, and over-provisioning could result in under-utilized resources and higher costs. With RDS storage autoscaling, you simply set your desired maximum storage limit for each additional storage volume, and autoscaling takes care of the rest.  
 RDS storage autoscaling continuously monitors actual storage consumption, and scales capacity up automatically when actual utilization approaches provisioned storage capacity. Autoscaling works with new and existing database instances. Autoscaling has no additional charges and you only pay for the provisioned

title: Amazon Aurora now supports post-quantum TLS key exchange
body:
Starting today,  Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition  introduces support for post-quantum TLS (PQ-TLS) key exchange, providing you with post-quantum cryptography options for encrypting your data in transit.  
 Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL versions 18 and higher support modification of the ssl_groups parameter. You can  select cryptographic groups  from the Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL allow list to align with your organization's security standards.  
 Amazon Aurora is designed for high performance and availability at global scale with full PostgreSQL compatibility. It provides scale-to-zero serverless compute, Aurora Global Database for multi-Region resilience, Aurora I/O-Optimized for improved price performance on I/O-intensive workloads, and built-in security and continuous backups. To get started, take a look at our  getting started page .

title: Amazon MSK Connect now supports updating connector plugins and worker configurations
body:
Amazon MSK Connect   (Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka Connect) now lets you update the custom plugin and worker configuration of an existing connector. This is useful when you need to update the custom plugin to run a new version of your connector code, for example one with updated dependencies. You can also update the worker configuration to change worker-level settings, such as switching key and value converters or tuning producer and consumer properties for throughput and latency.  
 Amazon MSK Connect is a fully managed service that allows you to deploy, monitor, and scale Apache Kafka Connect connectors with   Amazon MSK   (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka). Previously, updating a connector's plugin or worker configuration meant deleting the connector and recreating it - a disruptive operation that added risk and operational overhead. With this launch, you can update a connector's plugin and worker configuration in place. The connector keeps its committed offsets, so its tasks continue processing from where they left off once the update completes.

title: AWS Step Functions workflows now available as AI agent tools
body:
You can now use your AWS Step Functions workflows as tools for AI agents through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway. Your agent decides when to run a workflow and what input to pass, and Step Functions runs each step exactly as you defined it. Agents can use your existing Standard and Express workflows as tools. 
 AWS Step Functions is a visual workflow service capable of orchestrating over 220 AWS services to help customers build distributed applications at scale. AgentCore Gateway connects AI agents to tools through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). With this launch, your agents can run multi-step business processes in the same order every time. For example, a customer support agent can start your refund workflow, and Step Functions runs the eligibility check, manager approval, and credit steps, so every refund follows your policy. Agents can also look up workflow runs, so an operations agent can tell your on-call engineer which order runs failed overnight and where, letting them go straight to fixing the step that broke. 
 This capability is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway is available. You pay standard rates for Step Functions and AgentCore Gat

title: Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is now available in additional Regions
body:
Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is now available in two additional AWS Regions: Canada (Central) and Africa (Cape Town). DAX is a fully managed, highly available, in-memory cache for Amazon DynamoDB that delivers up to ten times performance improvement, from single-digit milliseconds to microseconds, even at millions of requests per second.  
 With DAX, you can accelerate read-intensive and bursty workloads such as real-time bidding, gaming leaderboards, and retail product catalogs, while offloading read traffic from your DynamoDB tables. DAX is API-compatible with DynamoDB, so you can add microsecond-latency caching to your applications with minimal code changes. Customers can now keep cached data within the Region and meet low-latency requirements while benefiting from a fully managed service, including automated patching and failover.  
 To learn more, see the  Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator page . For the full list of Regions where DAX is available, see the  AWS Regional Services page .

title: ACM now supports ACME for public certificates in AWS GovCloud (US)
body:
AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) ACME protocol support is now available in AWS GovCloud (US-East) and AWS GovCloud (US-West), providing a fully managed ACME server endpoint that issues public TLS certificates from Amazon Trust Services using any ACMEv2-compatible client, including Certbot, cert-manager for Kubernetes, and acme.sh. With the CA/Browser Forum mandating 47-day certificate lifetimes by 2029, manual management of public certificates becomes untenable. ACME support in ACM gives developers a standards-based path to fully automate certificate issuance and renewal. 
 To learn more, visit the  AWS News blog post , the  ACM ACME documentation , the  ACM pricing page , and the  AWS Regional Services page .

title: AWS DataSync Enhanced mode now supports Amazon FSx for Windows File Server, FSx for NetApp ONTAP, and Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization
body:
AWS DataSync Enhanced mode now supports Amazon FSx for Windows File Server and Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP as source or destination locations. You can now run Windows to Windows transfers, such as from an on-premises file server to FSx for Windows File Server. Additionally, Enhanced mode agents can now run on Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization version 4.20 or later.  
 With this launch, you can use the same location options in Enhanced mode as in Basic mode. Enhanced mode processes data in parallel for higher performance, removes file count limitations, and provides detailed data transfer metrics. OpenShift Virtualization expands your agent deployment options alongside VMware ESXi, KVM, Microsoft Hyper-V, and Amazon EC2.  
 You can get started by choosing Enhanced mode when you create a task in the  AWS DataSync console . These capabilities are available in all AWS Regions where DataSync Enhanced mode is supported. To learn more, visit the  AWS DataSync documentation .

title: Amazon SageMaker AI now supports SOCI-indexed images to start training jobs in seconds
body:
Today, Amazon SageMaker AI announces support for Seekable OCI (SOCI)-indexed container images for training and processing jobs, so your jobs start running your code sooner. SOCI-indexed images start Amazon SageMaker AI training containers in seconds, cutting GPU idle time during image pulls by up to 90%, with no impact on training performance. Before a training or processing job can run, SageMaker AI downloads its container image to the instance. For deep learning images, which routinely exceed 10 GB, that download adds minutes to the start of every job, and you pay for that time. Now, when your image includes a SOCI index, SageMaker AI lazy-loads the image, fetching only the files needed to start the container and streaming the rest in the background as your code runs.  
 To use this feature, reference a SOCI-indexed image from a private Amazon ECR repository in your training or processing job. You can use a pre-indexed AWS Deep Learning Container by changing the image tag to its -soci variant, or add a SOCI index to your own image in Amazon ECR with open-source tools, without rebuilding the image. No changes to your job definition, entry point, or data channels are needed. SageMa

title: Amazon Managed Grafana now supports in-place upgrade to Grafana version 13.2
body:
Amazon Managed Grafana now supports in-place upgrade from Grafana version 12.4 to 13.2. Upgrading to version 13.2 brings features launched as part of open-source Grafana versions 13.0 to 13.2. These include Git Sync for dashboards, dynamic dashboards, and PromQL query support in the Amazon CloudWatch data source plugin. 
 With Git Sync, you can treat dashboards as code by linking a workspace to a Git repository. Dashboard modifications can be tracked, reviewed, and reverted through version control. Dynamic dashboards bring a more adaptable approach to layout and paneling. You can construct responsive views driven by conditions that respond to the data and variables in scope. With Amazon CloudWatch data source plugin support for Prometheus Query Language, you can use PromQL to query metrics that CloudWatch takes in via its OpenTelemetry (OTLP) endpoint, in addition to the existing Metric Search and Metrics Insights query types. 
 In-place upgrade to Grafana 13.2 is supported in all  AWS regions  where Amazon Managed Grafana is generally available. You can upgrade with just a few clicks from the AWS Console, AWS SDK or AWS CLI. For a complete list of new features, refer to  Differenc

title: Amazon Redshift announces hands-off automated cross-region backups
body:
Amazon Redshift  announces automated cross-region snapshot copy for Amazon Redshift. You can now have your Amazon Redshift provisioned cluster or serverless workgroup automatically backed up to the target AWS region(s) you choose. The automated cross-region snapshot copy feature will automatically, always copy the most recent snapshot with no manual intervention, continuously and incrementally and ensure your cluster is backed-up to the destination region(s), giving you additional options for business continuity.  
 The benefit to enabling the new automated cross-region snapshot copy feature is that you do not need to manually intervene to initiate a cross-region snapshot copy when an unplanned outage event occurs. Also, this feature takes the most recent snapshot available on your system to copy to the destination region, so you don't have to wait for the next snapshot to be taken, making it independent of your snapshot schedule on your local cluster. To configure cross-region snapshot copy, you need to enable the automated cross-region snapshot copy feature for each cluster and configure the destination region(s) to copy snapshots and how long to keep copied automated snapshots i

title: AWS Backup now supports cross-account management and cross-account backup in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud
body:
AWS Backup now supports cross-account management, cross-account backup, and delegated administrators in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) Region. These capabilities help you centrally manage, monitor, and copy backups across the accounts in your organization using AWS Organizations.  
 With cross-account management, you can deploy organization-wide backup policies from your AWS Organizations management account or a delegated administrator account. You can also monitor backup, copy, and restore jobs across all of your organization accounts from one place. With cross-account backup, you can copy recovery points to a backup vault in another account in your organization, which adds protection against accidental or malicious deletion in the source account. You can also register a member account as a delegated administrator, so your teams can manage backups across your organization without needing access to your management account.  
 There is no additional charge to use these capabilities; standard AWS Backup pricing applies. To learn more, see the AWS Backup documentation at  https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/ . To get started, visit the AWS Backup console at  https://con

title: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio now supports custom designations
body:
Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio now supports custom designations, named permission sets that control what actions individual project members can perform. Previously, project members could only be assigned Owner or Contributor designations, which provided nearly identical permissions. With custom designations, administrators define permission sets that align with their organization's personas and assign them to project members. Designations govern all actions within a project, providing administrators with a single permission model for separation of duties. 
 Administrators create designations in the SageMaker Unified Studio administration portal by selecting permissions grouped into categories such as Catalog, Subscriptions, Connections, Notebooks, and Data Agent. For example, a "Data Steward" designation might include permissions to approve subscription requests and publish assets, while an "Analyst" designation is limited to querying data and running notebooks. Each designation is defined at the domain level and assigned across any project in that domain. When a member performs an action, SageMaker Unified Studio evaluates their assigned designation and permits or denies the requ

title: Amazon RDS for Oracle now supports September 2026 Monthly Recommended Patch
body:
Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for Oracle  now supports the September 2026 Monthly Recommended Patch (MRP) for Oracle Database version 19c and 26ai. An MRP is a minor engine version that builds on a quarterly Release Update (RU), bundling Oracle's Critical Security Patch Update (CSPU) with additional Oracle-recommended fixes. The September 2026 MRP is applied on top of the July 2026 RU and includes the  Oracle September CSPU . We recommend upgrading to the September 2026 MRP as it includes the latest security updates for Oracle Database.  
 This release also includes the updated Oracle time zone file (DST version 46), which reflects the latest daylight saving time rule changes in several regions, including British Columbia and Alberta in Canada (effective November 1, 2026) and Morocco and Western Sahara (effective September 20, 2026), which are moving to permanent UTC offsets. If you store timestamps that include time zone information for these areas, the updated time zone file keeps that data aligned with the new rules.  
 You can apply the September 2026 MRP for new database instances, or upgrade existing instances to engine version 19.0.0.0.ru-2026-07.mrp-2026-0

title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore CLI version 1.0 is now available
body:
AWS announces the general availability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore CLI version 1.0 (@aws/agentcore 1.0.0), rebuilt with faster startup, a consistent command structure, and support for more AgentCore resources. The CLI helps developers create, develop, deploy, and operate AI agents and supporting resources from the terminal.  
 With version 1.0, developers can use the project workflow or work directly with harnesses, runtimes, memory, identity, gateways, and payments without first adding them to a project. Developers can invoke existing resources by ID or ARN, open an interactive shell, export a harness, and use searchable menus, resource pickers, and guided workflows. Consistent global flags provide region selection, JSON output, debugging, and version information across commands.  
 Existing projects can be migrated to AgentCore version 1 using the agentcore migrate command.  
 Install AgentCore CLI version 1.0 from  npm  or explore the source on  GitHub . To learn more, visit the  Amazon Bedrock AgentCore product page ,  AgentCore CLI reference , and  Get started with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore .

title: Public endpoints for Amazon ElastiCache Serverless now in AWS GovCloud (US)
body:
Amazon ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey now supports public endpoints in the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. A public endpoint lets you connect to your cache from a serverless function or any application running outside a VPC, without setting up a VPN, a bastion host, or an SSH tunnel.  
 With a public endpoint, ElastiCache Serverless gives you a fully managed cache with no VPC to configure and no infrastructure to provision, and you can create one in under a minute. Every connection uses IAM authentication over TLS 1.3, so there's no password to store or rotate. Connect using Valkey GLIDE 2.2 or later, which has built-in IAM support, or another Valkey client paired with the Developer Toolkit for ElastiCache, an open-source library that generates and refreshes IAM authentication tokens for you.  
 With this expansion, public endpoints for ElastiCache Serverless are now available in all commercial AWS Regions, the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, and the China Regions. There is no additional charge for using public endpoints beyond standard ElastiCache Serverless pricing.

title: AWS Lambda supports Seekable OCI (SOCI) lazy loading for Lambda Managed Instances
body:
AWS Lambda now supports  Seekable OCI (SOCI)  for lazy loading  Event Functions  packaged as Open Container Initiative (OCI) images running on  Lambda Managed Instances . With SOCI support, Lambda fetches only the files needed at each stage of the execution environment startup rather than downloading the entire image upfront, reducing container startup times by up to 70%.  
 Customers building compute-intensive applications such as data processing pipelines, high-throughput API backends, and batch computation workloads require substantial memory and CPU resources to process large datasets, serve low-latency responses at scale, and run complex computations efficiently. Container images for these workloads can reach several gigabytes, and downloading and preparing the full image can take several minutes when provisioning new execution environments. SOCI support on Lambda Managed Instances eliminates this bottleneck by streaming only the required files at each stage of the execution environment startup, so your functions start faster as you scale.  
 To get started, create a  SOCI index  (a table of contents for the files in your image layers) for your container image and pu

title: Introducing time series collections for the next generation of Amazon OpenSearch Serverless
body:
Today, we're announcing support for time series collections on the next generation of Amazon OpenSearch Serverless. With time series collections, you can ingest, store, and analyze logs, metrics, traces, and event data without provisioning or managing clusters. They absorb ingest spikes automatically, keep recent data fast to query, and make months or years of history searchable at low cost, all in the same collection.  
 Time series collections add a new, lower-cost warm storage tier in addition to the existing hot storage tier, so customers can retain their infrequently accessed data without paying hot storage prices. Customers can choose how long data stays hot before transitiong to warm storage.  With up to 100 TB of hot storage per collection, time series collections can handle high-volume observability workloads such as application monitoring, security analytics, and IoT telemetry. Alerting and anomaly detection are also now available, so customers can get notified about issues and spot unusual patterns in their log and event data without separate tooling.  
 Time series collections are available today in all  AWS Regions  where OpenSearch Serverless is available. To lea

title: Quick now supports smart approvals for agentic actions
body:
Amazon Quick now supports smart approvals, a review layer that reduces unnecessary approval prompts while preserving human oversight of the actions that matter most. As agents take more actions on a user's behalf, such as sending email, updating records, and creating tickets, asking a person to approve every step leads to approval fatigue and weaker oversight over time. With smart approvals, a separate review model called the classifier evaluates each eligible action against the user's request. It approves routine actions automatically and refers consequential actions to the user for review.  
 Your existing policies always come first. Smart approvals only reviews actions where the user's setting is "ask" each time. Denied actions stay denied, and smart approvals never grants new access. The classifier sends higher-impact actions to the user for review. These include sending content outside the organization, changing permissions, deleting content, making payments, and actions that go beyond what the user asked for. Each automatic approval covers only the exact action that was reviewed. If a review fails or times out, the action goes to the user.  
 Smart approvals is on for all use

title: Amazon EKS Dashboard now provides fleet-wide visibility into certificate authority (CA) rotation
body:
Today, Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) announces certificate authority (CA) rotation visibility in the Amazon EKS Dashboard, giving you a consolidated view of CA rotation across your clusters. The Amazon EKS Dashboard already provides centralized visibility into your clusters across AWS Regions and accounts, and it now includes CA rotation, so you can see where action is needed without checking each cluster individually.  
 Each Amazon EKS cluster has its own CA, and clusters created since 2018 have CAs with a 10-year validity period that are now approaching the point where rotation activities should begin. In the EKS Dashboard, you can now see your clusters and their CA rotation status, which clusters have CAs approaching expiration, and upcoming automated rotation events, so platform teams who operate many clusters can prioritize action across their fleet from one place.  
 The Amazon EKS Dashboard aggregates data across your accounts and Regions through AWS Organizations, so you enable trusted access for the dashboard in your organization’s management account to use this capability. You view the dashboard from the US East region (us-east-1), and it is available at

title: Amazon ECS Managed Instances adds cross-instance and Spot consolidation
body:
Today,  Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) Managed Instances  introduces two infrastructure optimization updates: cross-instance and Spot consolidation. Cross-instance consolidation evaluates tasks running across multiple underutilized instances together, packing them onto fewer instances to raise utilization and lower costs. Spot consolidation extends this capability to Spot capacity, consolidating underutilized Spot Instances after first verifying replacement capacity is available. 
 Amazon ECS Managed Instances provisions, configures, and operates right-sized Amazon EC2 instances for your workloads, balancing availability and cost. Its infrastructure optimization continuously monitors your fleet, reclaiming idle capacity and consolidating underutilized instances with graceful start-before-stop task replacement. Until now, optimization evaluated each instance in isolation for replacement, which worked well when a capacity provider was configured with diverse instance types. However, when a capacity provider was configured with a narrow range of instance types, there were fewer opportunities to consolidate multiple underutilized instances, because no single replacement

title: AWS Lambda durable functions now exports live telemetry for execution insights
body:
AWS Lambda announces the Durable Execution Telemetry Exporter plugin for Lambda durable functions. This new observability plugin captures the step-by-step history of your durable executions and sends them to one or more destinations of your choice. You can use the exported data to gather operational and business insights and keep history beyond the standard retention period. We are also releasing a companion Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that lets AI agents such as Kiro query your exported telemetry data using natural language.  
 Lambda durable functions helps you build resilient multi-step applications and AI workflows that run for up to one year. The new Telemetry Exporter sends data such as execution status, operation timing, step input and output, and errors to 13 built-in destinations. Destinations include Amazon CloudWatch Logs, Amazon S3 for Amazon Athena, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon Aurora, and Amazon OpenSearch Service. You can redact sensitive fields before export and set a sampling rate to control data volume.
